correctness.rationale: Deleting the hub leaves directed paths, so the off-hub block contributes determinant 1 and the Schur complement is one minus the first-return series. The Perron equation has exactly one root greater than one by strict decrease of the sum of inverse powers; a common root there is exactly the condition for equal entropy. The independent exhaustive rational gcd/Sturm check confirms 82 pair comparisons through 9 vertices with loops allowed and 69 through 11 without loops. It finds only the respective boundary pairs (1,4,6)/(2,2,7) and (2,5,6)/(3,3,7). Their gcds are (x+1)(x^3-x^2-1) and x^3-x-1, respectively. Repeated lengths are allowed; repeated self-loops are not. Each of the four triples has gcd one, so the shifts are mixing. The first pair has fixed-point counts 1 and 0; the second has counts 2 and 0 for fixed points of the squared shift. Thus neither pair is conjugate.
residual_risks: Only the finite equal-order three-petal classifications in the stated loop regimes are established. The uploaded checker was inspected but not executed.

value.rationale: Three petals are a natural next test of entropy rigidity after two-return sparse digraphs. The classification pins down exactly where entropy loses the return multiset at fixed order, and shows that forbidding self-loops moves the threshold rather than restoring rigidity. The explicit mixing nonconjugate witnesses and the exclusion of all earlier pairs give a useful sharp baseline for extensions beyond three returns.
residual_risks: This is not a rigidity classification of all excess-two digraphs or of all finite shifts of equal entropy.
